at gabe.explanation: "At gabe" means "to yawn", to open your mouth wide when you are sleepy or bored. It also describes a big opening: Hullet gaber (The hole gapes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke lade være med at **gabe**, når jeg er træt.
sentence.en: I cannot help yawning when I am tired.

at gange.explanation: "At gange" means "to multiply": Jeg ganger to med tre (I multiply two by three). It comes from gange (times): Tre gange to er seks (Three times two is six).

sentence.da: I skolen lærer vi at **gange** og dividere.
sentence.en: At school we learn to multiply and divide.

at garantere.explanation: "At garantere" means "to guarantee", to promise firmly that something is true or will happen. It is stronger than at love (to promise), because you are saying that you are completely sure.

sentence.da: Butikken vil **garantere**, at varen kan sendes tilbage inden for tredive dage.
sentence.en: The store will guarantee that the item can be sent back within thirty days.

at gemme.explanation: "At gemme" means "to save", like a file or something you keep for later: Jeg gemmer filen (I am saving the file). It can also mean "to hide": Hun gemte nøglen (She hid the key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gemme** billedet på min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to save the picture on my phone.

at gemme sig.explanation: "At gemme sig" means "to hide": Børnene gemmer sig bag sofaen (The kids hide behind the sofa). To hide an object, use at gemme without sig: Jeg gemmer nøglen (I hide the key).

sentence.da: Katten plejer at **gemme sig** under sengen.
sentence.en: The cat usually hides under the bed.

at genbruge.explanation: "At genbruge" means "to recycle" or "to reuse": Vi genbruger flasker (We recycle bottles). Gen- means "again", so it is bruge (to use) again.

sentence.da: Papir og glas kan man **genbruge**.
sentence.en: Paper and glass can be recycled.

at generalisere.explanation: "At generalisere" means "to generalize", to treat something that is true for a few cases as true for all of them. It often comes in a warning that something does not hold for everyone.

sentence.da: Man kan ikke **generalisere** ud fra kun to eksempler.
sentence.en: You cannot generalize from only two examples.

at genere.explanation: "At genere" means "to bother", when something or someone is unpleasant or in your way. It is often used politely: Generer jeg dig? (Am I bothering you?)

sentence.da: Musikken kan **genere** naboerne om natten.
sentence.en: The music can bother the neighbors at night.

at gengive.explanation: "At gengive" means "to reproduce" or "to render": to tell or show again what someone said or wrote, staying close to the original. It also fits a picture or a text that shows something: Maleriet gengiver en storm (The painting shows a storm).

sentence.da: En god journalist skal **gengive** politikerens ord præcist.
sentence.en: A good journalist must reproduce the politician's words exactly.

at genkende.explanation: "At genkende" means "to recognize", when you know someone or something from before: Jeg genkender din stemme (I recognize your voice). It is built from gen (again) and kende (to know), and gen is also in at genbruge (to reuse).

sentence.da: Kan du **genkende** manden på billedet?
sentence.en: Can you recognize the man in the picture?

at gennemføre.explanation: "At gennemføre" means "to carry out", to take a plan, a test or a course through all its steps until it is done. Gennem means "through", so you go through the whole thing, not just the start.

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **gennemføre** planen og bygge en ny skole.
sentence.en: The municipality will carry out the plan and build a new school.

at gennemgå.explanation: "At gennemgå" means "to go through" or "to review", to take things one by one, such as a text, a lesson or a list, often to explain them. It can also mean to live through something hard: Hun har gennemgået en stor operation (She has been through a major operation).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **gennemgå** opgaverne med klassen i morgen.
sentence.en: The teacher will go through the exercises with the class tomorrow.

at gennemskue.explanation: "At gennemskue" means "to see through": to understand what is really going on behind a trick, a lie or a person's plan. It is about figuring something out, not about looking through glass: Jeg gennemskuede hans løgn (I saw through his lie).

sentence.da: Politiet kunne hurtigt **gennemskue** svindlerens plan.
sentence.en: The police could quickly see through the swindler's plan.

at genopbygge.explanation: "At genopbygge" means "to rebuild", to build up again something that was destroyed or damaged, such as a house after a fire or a city after a war. Gen- at the start means "again", as in at genstarte (to restart).

sentence.da: Efter branden vil de **genopbygge** huset på samme sted.
sentence.en: After the fire they will rebuild the house in the same place.

at genoplive.explanation: "At genoplive" means "to revive", to bring someone back to life, or to bring something forgotten back into use, such as an old tradition. Gen- means "again", as in at genskabe (to recreate).

sentence.da: Lægen forsøgte at **genoplive** manden efter hjertestoppet.
sentence.en: The doctor tried to revive the man after the cardiac arrest.

at genoprette.explanation: "At genoprette" means "to restore": to bring back a normal state that was lost, such as order, contact or power. For an old building or painting, the word is at restaurere (to restore).

sentence.da: Politiet skal **genoprette** roen efter urolighederne.
sentence.en: The police must restore calm after the riots.

at genoptage.explanation: "At genoptage" means "to resume", to take up something again after it was paused, such as work after a break or a meeting after lunch. Gen- means "again", as in at genoverveje (to reconsider).

sentence.da: Vi vil **genoptage** mødet efter frokost.
sentence.en: We will resume the meeting after lunch.

at genoverveje.explanation: "At genoverveje" means "to reconsider": gen- means "again", and at overveje (to consider) is to think a choice over. So you think over a decision a second time, often before you change it.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **genoverveje** tilbuddet og svare dig i morgen.
sentence.en: I will reconsider the offer and answer you tomorrow.

at genskabe.explanation: "At genskabe" means "to recreate" or "to restore", to make something exist again the way it was, such as a mood, a lost file or a design. It also covers repeating something so that you get the same result as before.

sentence.da: Forskerne kunne ikke **genskabe** resultatet i deres eget laboratorium.
sentence.en: The researchers could not recreate the result in their own laboratory.

at genstarte.explanation: "At genstarte" means "to restart", to turn something off and on again, most often a computer, a phone or a router. It also works for a project or a series that begins anew.

sentence.da: Hvis skærmen fryser, kan du **genstarte** computeren.
sentence.en: If the screen freezes, you can restart the computer.

at gentage.explanation: "At gentage" means "to repeat", to say or do something again: Jeg gentager mit spørgsmål (I repeat my question). It also works for events: Historien gentager sig (History repeats itself).

sentence.da: Kan du **gentage** det langsomt, tak?
sentence.en: Can you repeat that slowly, please?

at gide.explanation: "At gide" means "to be bothered to", and it is about having the energy or will. It is mostly used with ikke or in questions: Jeg gider ikke (I can't be bothered). Gider du komme med? (Do you feel like coming along?)

sentence.da: Han vil nok ikke **gide** at hjælpe os.
sentence.en: He probably won't feel like helping us.

at gifte sig.explanation: "At gifte sig" means "to get married". The little word sig changes to match who is marrying: du gifter dig (you get married), han gifter sig (he gets married). Gift on its own means "married": Jeg er gift (I am married).

sentence.da: De vil **gifte sig** i kirken.
sentence.en: They want to get married in the church.

at give.explanation: "At give" means "to give": Jeg giver dig bogen (I give you the book). It is part of many phrases, such as at give op (to give up) and at give besked (to let someone know).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **give** dig en gave.
sentence.en: I want to give you a present.

at give afkald på.explanation: "At give afkald på" means "to renounce" or "to give up": to choose not to use something you have a right to, such as money, a claim or a pleasure. It is your own choice, not a loss: Hun gav afkald på sin løn (She gave up her pay).

sentence.da: Man kan **give afkald på** sin arv og lade andre få den.
sentence.en: You can renounce your inheritance and let others get it.

at give besked.explanation: "At give besked" means "to let someone know": Giv mig besked i morgen (Let me know tomorrow). To be the one who is told, use at få besked (to be notified).

sentence.da: Kan du **give besked**, når du er fremme?
sentence.en: Can you let me know when you arrive?

at give efter.explanation: "At give efter" means "to give in": to stop resisting and let the other person have their way. It is also used for things that bend or break under pressure: Isen gav efter (The ice gave way).

sentence.da: Forældrene vil ikke **give efter**, selv om barnet græder.
sentence.en: The parents will not give in, even though the child is crying.

at give en hånd med.explanation: "At give en hånd med" means "to give a hand", or "to help out": Kan du give en hånd med? (Can you lend a hand?) Literally it is to give a hand along: med (along) means you join in on a job that someone is already doing.

forms.da: jeg har givet en hånd med

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **give en hånd med** flytningen.
sentence.en: We would like to give a hand with the move.

at give lov.explanation: "At give lov" means "to give permission": Min mor gav mig lov (My mom gave me permission). Lov on its own also means "law", but in this phrase it is permission.

sentence.da: Far vil nok **give lov**, når vi spørger pænt.
sentence.en: Dad will probably give permission when we ask nicely.

at give op.explanation: "At give op" means "to give up", when you stop trying: Jeg giver ikke op (I am not giving up). Op (up) is a small word that changes the verb in many phrases: at skrive op (to write down), at ringe op (to call up).

sentence.da: Det er svært, men jeg vil ikke **give op**.
sentence.en: It is hard, but I won't give up.

at give sig.explanation: "At give sig" means "to give in" or "to yield". You mostly hear it in the negative, for someone who will not back down: Jeg giver mig ikke (I will not back down). It also describes pain or weather that eases off: Smerterne giver sig (The pain eases off).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **give sig**, før hun har fået et svar.
sentence.en: She will not back down until she has an answer.

at give tilbage.explanation: "At give tilbage" means "to give back": Han gav mig pengene tilbage (He gave me the money back). To take something back to a shop or library, use at returnere (to return).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **give tilbage**, hvad jeg har lånt.
sentence.en: I want to give back what I borrowed.

at glemme.explanation: "At glemme" means "to forget", both facts and things you were meant to bring or do: Jeg glemte at ringe (I forgot to call).

sentence.da: Jeg må ikke **glemme** min paraply.
sentence.en: I must not forget my umbrella.

at glide.explanation: "At glide" means "to slide" or "to slip", to move smoothly over a surface, like a boat on water. It can also be an accident: Kniven gled (The knife slipped).

sentence.da: Skøjteløberen kan **glide** hen over isen uden at anstrenge sig.
sentence.en: The skater can glide across the ice without any effort.

at glo.explanation: "At glo" means "to stare", looking at someone or something for too long with fixed eyes. It is everyday speech and often sounds critical: Hvad glor du på? (What are you staring at?) means roughly "Stop looking at me".

sentence.da: Det er uhøfligt at **glo** på folk.
sentence.en: It is rude to stare at people.

at glæde.explanation: "At glæde" means "to please" or "to delight", to give someone a good feeling. Do not mix it up with at glæde sig til (to look forward to), where sig makes you the one who feels it: Jeg glæder mig til ferien (I look forward to the vacation).

sentence.da: Det vil **glæde** mormor meget at se dig.
sentence.en: It will please grandma a lot to see you.

at glæde sig over.explanation: "At glæde sig over" means "to be happy about" something that is here now: Jeg glæder mig over gaven (I am happy about the gift). For the future, use at glæde sig til (to look forward to): Jeg glæder mig til ferien (I look forward to the vacation).

sentence.da: Hun kan **glæde sig over** de små ting i livet.
sentence.en: She can be happy about the small things in life.

at glæde sig til.explanation: "At glæde sig til" means "to look forward to": Jeg glæder mig til weekenden (I look forward to the weekend). Sig changes with the person: Vi glæder os til festen (We look forward to the party).

sentence.da: Børnene begynder at **glæde sig til** sommerferien.
sentence.en: The children are starting to look forward to the summer vacation.

at gløde.explanation: "At gløde" means "to glow", to give off a steady warm light, like hot coals or metal heated in a fire. It also describes a person who beams with joy: Hun gløder af stolthed (She glows with pride).

sentence.da: Jernet skal **gløde**, før smeden kan forme det.
sentence.en: The iron must glow before the smith can shape it.

at gnave.explanation: "At gnave" means "to gnaw": to bite at something hard again and again, as mice and dogs do. It also works for a worry that will not leave you alone: Tanken gnavede i mig (The thought gnawed at me).

sentence.da: Hunden vil **gnave** på knoglen hele dagen.
sentence.en: The dog wants to gnaw on the bone all day.

at gnide.explanation: "At gnide" means "to rub", to press something against a surface and move it back and forth. Adding ind makes it "to rub in": at gnide creme ind (to rub in cream).

sentence.da: Hun må **gnide** sine kolde hænder for at få varmen.
sentence.en: She has to rub her cold hands to get warm.

at godkende.explanation: "At godkende" means "to approve", to officially say yes to something so it may go ahead, such as a plan, a budget, an application or a medicine.

sentence.da: Chefen skal **godkende** budgettet, før vi bruger penge.
sentence.en: The boss has to approve the budget before we spend money.

at godtage.explanation: "At godtage" means "to accept" something, like an explanation, an offer or a rule: Jeg kan ikke godtage forklaringen (I cannot accept the explanation).

sentence.da: Vi kan ikke **godtage** den høje pris.
sentence.en: We cannot accept the high price.

at google.explanation: "At google" means "to google", to search for something online: Jeg googler åbningstiderne (I google the opening hours).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **google** en opskrift på pandekager.
sentence.en: I want to google a recipe for pancakes.

at grave.explanation: "At grave" means "to dig", making a hole in the ground: Hunden graver i haven (The dog is digging in the garden). With op (up) it means digging something out: grave noget op (dig something up).

sentence.da: Med en spade kan man **grave** et dybt hul.
sentence.en: With a spade you can dig a deep hole.

at gribe.explanation: "At gribe" means "to grab" and "to catch" something that is thrown: Hun greb bolden (She caught the ball). Han greb min arm (He grabbed my arm).

sentence.da: Kan du **gribe** bolden, når jeg kaster den?
sentence.en: Can you catch the ball when I throw it?

at gribe ind.explanation: "At gribe ind" means "to intervene", to step into a situation and change what is happening. The root at gribe means "to grab" or "to catch", and ind (in) gives the picture of reaching into the situation.

sentence.da: Læreren må **gribe ind**, når børnene begynder at slås.
sentence.en: The teacher has to intervene when the children start fighting.

at grille.explanation: "At grille" means "to grill", to cook food over hot coals, gas or electricity, usually outdoors. You can use it without naming the food: Vi griller i aften (We are grilling tonight).

sentence.da: Vi kan **grille** pølser i haven, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: We can grill sausages in the garden when it is warm.

at grine.explanation: "At grine" means "to laugh", usually out loud at something funny: Vi grinede meget (We laughed a lot). Be careful with grine af (to laugh at someone), which can mean mocking them: Hvorfor griner du af mig? (Why are you laughing at me?)

sentence.da: Børnene vil **grine** af den sjove klovn.
sentence.en: The children want to laugh at the funny clown.

at gro.explanation: "At gro" means "to grow", for things that come up out of the ground or skin, such as plants, moss and hair: Der gror mos på taget (Moss is growing on the roof). For a child getting taller or something getting bigger, use at vokse (to grow bigger).

sentence.da: Tomater kan **gro** i et drivhus, når det er koldt ude.
sentence.en: Tomatoes can grow in a greenhouse when it is cold outside.

at gruble.explanation: "At gruble" means "to brood" or "to ponder": to think about something for a long time, often with worry and without getting anywhere. Use over for the topic: Jeg grubler over, hvad jeg skal gøre (I am brooding over what to do).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ligge vågen og **gruble** over mine problemer.
sentence.en: I can lie awake and brood over my problems.

at gruppere.explanation: "At gruppere" means "to group", to put people or things into groups that share something, such as age, size or topic.

sentence.da: Læreren vil **gruppere** eleverne efter niveau.
sentence.en: The teacher will group the students by level.

at græde.explanation: "At græde" means "to cry", shedding tears from sadness, pain or even joy: Hvorfor græder du? (Why are you crying?)

sentence.da: Barnet er ked af det og vil **græde**.
sentence.en: The child is sad and wants to cry.

at gynge.explanation: "At gynge" means "to swing", to move gently back and forth or up and down, like a boat on waves or a child in the playground. To swing a bat or a golf club is at svinge, not at gynge.

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at **gynge** på legepladsen.
sentence.en: The children love to swing at the playground.

at gå.explanation: "At gå" means "to go on foot", so to walk, and also "to leave": Jeg går nu (I am leaving now). It also describes how things are going (Det går godt means "It is going well") and buses and trains that run (Bussen går hver time means "The bus runs every hour"). For going by car or plane, use at køre (to drive) or at flyve (to fly) instead.

sentence.da: Vi vil hellere **gå** end køre.
sentence.en: We would rather walk than drive.

at gå af.explanation: "At gå af" means "to resign", for someone who leaves a post such as a minister or a boss. It also has two everyday uses: "to get off" a bus or train, and "to go off", like an alarm clock: Alarmen gik af (The alarm went off).

sentence.da: Direktøren vil **gå af**, når året er slut.
sentence.en: The director will resign when the year is over.

at gå agurk.explanation: "At gå agurk" means "to go crazy": to go to pieces from stress, anger or excitement. Literally it is to go cucumber. It is everyday slang, used among friends and family rather than in formal writing.

forms.da: Jeg er ved at gå agurk
forms.en: I am about to go crazy

sentence.da: Jeg kan **gå agurk**, når børnene larmer hele dagen.
sentence.en: I could go crazy when the children make noise all day.

at gå amok.explanation: "At gå amok" means "to go berserk": to stop controlling yourself and act wildly, often with anger or violence. It is also used for a crowd or an animal that cannot be held back.

sentence.da: Tyren kan **gå amok** og løbe ind i folkemængden.
sentence.en: The bull can go berserk and run into the crowd.

at gå en tur.explanation: "At gå en tur" means "to go for a walk", just for pleasure or fresh air. You can add where: gå en tur i parken (go for a walk in the park). En tur can also mean "a trip", as in en tur til Aarhus (a trip to Aarhus), so the situation tells you which is meant.

forms.en: I have been for a walk

sentence.da: Efter maden vil vi **gå en tur**.
sentence.en: After the meal we want to go for a walk.

at gå forbi.explanation: "At gå forbi" means "to pass by" on foot: Jeg går forbi skolen hver dag (I walk past the school every day). Forbi (past) works with other verbs too: køre forbi (drive past).

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **gå forbi** bageren på vej hjem.
sentence.en: I usually pass the bakery on the way home.

at gå fra hinanden.explanation: "At gå fra hinanden" means "to break up", literally "to go from each other". It is used when two people end a relationship together: Vi gik fra hinanden i går (We broke up yesterday).

sentence.da: Efter tre år besluttede de at **gå fra hinanden**.
sentence.en: After three years they decided to break up.

at gå galt.explanation: "At gå galt" means "to go wrong" and is about plans and events: Alt gik galt i går (Everything went wrong yesterday). For a wrong answer, use forkert (wrong) instead.

sentence.da: Det kan **gå galt**, når vejen er glat.
sentence.en: It can go wrong when the road is slippery.

at gå glip af.explanation: "At gå glip af" means "to miss out on" something you wanted to be part of: Jeg gik glip af festen (I missed out on the party). For a bus, Danes say Jeg missede bussen (I missed the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **gå glip af** koncerten.
sentence.en: I don't want to miss out on the concert.

at gå hjem.explanation: "At gå hjem" means "to go home", usually on foot: Jeg går hjem nu (I am going home now). By car, say at køre hjem (to drive home). At tage hjem (to head home) works whatever way you travel.

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **gå hjem**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to go home.

at gå i biografen.explanation: "At gå i biografen" means "to go to the movies". Literally it is "to go in the movie theater", and it is the normal phrase however you get there. You can also say the shorter at gå i bio (to go to the movies).

forms.en: I have gone to the movies

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå i biografen** i aften.
sentence.en: We want to go to the movies tonight.

at gå i gang med.explanation: "At gå i gang med" means "to get started on", for beginning a task. Med comes before what you start: Hun gik i gang med maden (She got started on the food). Leave it out when nothing follows: Vi er gået i gang (We have started).

forms.da: jeg er gået i gang med

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå i gang med** opgaven nu.
sentence.en: We have to get started on the task now.

at gå i panik.explanation: "At gå i panik" means "to panic", literally "to go into panic": Hun gik i panik, da lyset gik (She panicked when the lights went out). The calm opposite is at bevare roen (to stay calm).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **gå i panik**, for vi har god tid.
sentence.en: Don't panic, because we have plenty of time.

at gå i seng.explanation: "At gå i seng" means "to go to bed": Godnat, jeg går i seng (Good night, I am going to bed). Falling asleep is something different: at falde i søvn (to fall asleep).

sentence.da: Børnene er trætte og skal **gå i seng**.
sentence.en: The children are tired and have to go to bed.

at gå i stykker.explanation: "At gå i stykker" means "to break": Min telefon gik i stykker (My phone broke). It is for something that falls apart or stops working. To break it yourself, use at ødelægge (to destroy): Jeg ødelagde telefonen (I broke the phone).

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel kan nemt **gå i stykker**.
sentence.en: The old bike can easily break.

at gå i stå.explanation: "At gå i stå" means "to come to a standstill": to stop working or stop moving forward, for a machine or a process. It also describes a person whose mind suddenly goes blank: Jeg gik helt i stå (My mind went completely blank).

forms.en: it has come to a standstill

sentence.da: Arbejdet kan **gå i stå**, når pengene slipper op.
sentence.en: The work can come to a standstill when the money runs out.

at gå igennem.explanation: "At gå igennem" means "to go through", passing from one side of a place to the other: Vi gik igennem skoven (We went through the forest). It also means "to go over" something, checking it step by step: Vi går opgaven igennem (We go over the task).

sentence.da: Vi kan **gå igennem** tunnelen til den anden side.
sentence.en: We can go through the tunnel to the other side.

at gå ind.explanation: "At gå ind" means "to go in", walking into a place such as a room or a house. Danish has two little words: ind for going in, and inde for being inside: Han er inde i huset (He is inside the house).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå ind** i huset nu.
sentence.en: We have to go into the house now.

at gå ind for.explanation: "At gå ind for" means "to be in favor of", to back an idea, a proposal or a rule and want it to happen. Its opposite is at gå imod (to go against): Jeg går imod forslaget (I am against the proposal).

forms.en: I have been in favor of

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gå ind for** forslaget, hvis prisen er rimelig.
sentence.en: I will support the proposal if the price is reasonable.

at gå med til.explanation: "At gå med til" means "to agree to", to say yes to a plan or a request, often after first being unsure. Med (with) shows you are going along with what someone else wants.

sentence.da: Han ville ikke **gå med til** at sælge huset.
sentence.en: He did not want to agree to sell the house.

at gå ned.explanation: "At gå ned" means "to go down", moving to a lower place, such as a basement or down a hill. It is also used for the sun: solen går ned means "the sun sets".

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå ned** ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to walk down the stairs.

at gå op.explanation: "At gå op" means "to go up", moving to a higher place, such as an upper floor or up a hill. It is also used for the sun: solen går op means "the sun rises".

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå op** ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to walk up the stairs.

at gå op for.explanation: "At gå op for" means "to dawn on", for the moment when someone suddenly realizes something. The person who realizes it comes after for: Det gik op for mig, at jeg tog fejl (It dawned on me that I was wrong).

forms.da: det er gået op for mig

sentence.da: Det vil snart **gå op for** dig, hvor svært det er.
sentence.en: It will soon dawn on you how hard it is.

at gå over åen efter vand.explanation: "At gå over åen efter vand" means "to make things unnecessarily complicated". The picture is crossing a stream to fetch water when there is water close by. People say it when someone takes a long way to something simple.

forms.da: Du går over åen efter vand
forms.en: You are making things unnecessarily complicated

forms.da: Lad os ikke gå over åen efter vand
Hvorfor gå over åen efter vand?
forms.en: Why take the long way round?

related.da: at gøre en myg til en elefant
related.en: to make a mountain out of a molehill

sentence.da: Det er dumt at **gå over åen efter vand**, når løsningen er nem.
sentence.en: It is silly to make things unnecessarily complicated when the solution is easy.

at gå på café.explanation: "At gå på café" means "to go to a café". Danish says på café (literally on café) with no en (a), and the same goes for på restaurant (to a restaurant).

forms.en: I have gone to a café

related.en: to go out on the town

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå på café** i dag.
sentence.en: We want to go to a café today.

at gå på nerverne.explanation: "At gå på nerverne" means "to get on someone's nerves": to annoy someone a lot, often with something that keeps going, like a noise or a habit. The annoyed person comes after går: Larmen går mig på nerverne (The noise gets on my nerves).

forms.da: jeg er gået ham på nerverne
forms.en: I have gotten on his nerves

sentence.da: Lyden fra en dryppende vandhane kan **gå på nerverne**.
sentence.en: The sound of a dripping faucet can get on your nerves.

at gå på pension.explanation: "At gå på pension" means "to retire", to stop working for good, usually because of age. På (on) shows that you move onto a pension.

sentence.da: Min far vil **gå på pension**, når han bliver 67.
sentence.en: My father will retire when he turns 67.

at gå rundt.explanation: "At gå rundt" means "to walk around", with no fixed goal: Vi gik rundt i byen hele dagen (We walked around town all day). With om it means "around something": Vi gik rundt om søen (We walked around the lake).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **gå rundt** og se på butikkerne.
sentence.en: I would like to walk around and look at the stores.

at gå som katten om den varme grød.explanation: "At gå som katten om den varme grød" means "to beat around the bush": to stay away from the main subject. The picture is a cat circling hot porridge without daring to eat it. People say it when someone talks about everything except the real issue.

forms.da: Du går som katten om den varme grød
forms.en: You are beating around the bush

forms.da: Gå ikke som katten om den varme grød
forms.en: Do not beat around the bush

forms.da: Hun gik som katten om den varme grød

sentence.da: Han vil **gå som katten om den varme grød** i stedet for at svare.
sentence.en: He wants to beat around the bush instead of answering.

at gå som smurt.explanation: "At gå som smurt" means "to go smoothly", used for plans, trips and tasks that run without any trouble. Smurt is from at smøre (to grease), so it is like a machine that runs well because it is oiled.

sentence.da: Hvis vi forbereder os godt, vil prøven **gå som smurt**.
sentence.en: If we prepare well, the test will go smoothly.

at gå tabt.explanation: "At gå tabt" means "to be lost", for something that disappears and is not found again, such as a file, a letter or a chance. The thing disappears by itself. When you are the one who loses it, you say at miste (to lose): Jeg mistede min nøgle (I lost my key).

sentence.da: Hvis computeren går i stykker, kan data **gå tabt**.
sentence.en: If the computer breaks, data can be lost.

at gå til.explanation: "At gå til" means "to go to (regularly)", for a hobby or class you attend every week, with the activity right after: Jeg går til svømning (I go to swimming lessons). It also appears in Hvordan gik det til? (How did that happen?).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **gå til** fodbold, ligesom sin storebror.
sentence.en: He would like to play soccer, just like his big brother.

at gå til eksamen.explanation: "At gå til eksamen" means "to take an exam", sitting a test at school or university. It is for the exam itself, not studying for it: Hun går til eksamen i juni (She takes her exam in June).

sentence.da: Jeg har læst meget, og nu skal jeg **gå til eksamen**.
sentence.en: I have studied a lot, and now I have to take the exam.

at gå tilbage.explanation: "At gå tilbage" means "to go back", returning to where you came from: Jeg går tilbage til hotellet (I walk back to the hotel). This one is for going on foot. By car, say at køre tilbage (to drive back).

sentence.da: Nu skal vi **gå tilbage** til stationen.
sentence.en: Now we have to walk back to the station.

at gå ud.explanation: "At gå ud" means "to go out", either to leave a place such as the house, or to go out for the evening, for example to a bar or restaurant: Skal vi gå ud? (Shall we go out?).

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå ud** i haven nu.
sentence.en: We want to go out into the garden now.

at gå ud fra.explanation: "At gå ud fra" means "to assume", taking something as true without checking: Jeg går ud fra, at du har tid (I assume you have time).

sentence.da: Vi må **gå ud fra**, at han kommer.
sentence.en: We have to assume that he is coming.

at gå ud med.explanation: "At gå ud med" means "to go out with", as in dating someone: Hun går ud med Peter (She is going out with Peter). It also means taking something out: Jeg går ud med hunden (I am taking the dog out).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **gå ud med** hende, fordi han kan lide hende.
sentence.en: He would like to go out with her because he likes her.

at gå videre.explanation: "At gå videre" means "to move on", going on to the next thing: Nu går vi videre til næste side (Now we move on to the next page). It also fits life: Hun er gået videre (She has moved on).

sentence.da: Efter pausen skal vi **gå videre** til næste emne.
sentence.en: After the break we move on to the next topic.

at gå væk.explanation: "At gå væk" means "to go away" or "to walk off", leaving a place. As a command, Gå væk! means "Go away!", a blunt order like "Get lost!", so be careful.

sentence.da: Katten vil **gå væk** fra hunden.
sentence.en: The cat wants to go away from the dog.

at gætte.explanation: "At gætte" means "to guess", giving an answer without knowing it for sure. To name your guess, add på: Jeg gætter på Peter (I am guessing Peter). Gæt hvad! means "Guess what!".

sentence.da: Kan du **gætte** min alder?
sentence.en: Can you guess my age?

at gø.explanation: "At gø" means "to bark", and it is used for dogs: Hunden gøede hele natten (The dog barked all night). The present form gør looks exactly like gør from at gøre (to do), so the sentence tells you which one it is.

sentence.da: Hunden må ikke **gø** om natten.
sentence.en: The dog is not allowed to bark at night.

at gøre.explanation: "At gøre" means "to do", as in Hvad gør du? (What are you doing?). It can stand in for an action you do not want to repeat: Jeg læser, og det gør hun også (I am reading, and she does too). For making things, such as food, Danish uses at lave (to make): at lave mad (to cook).

sentence.da: Hvad vil du **gøre** i dag?
sentence.en: What do you want to do today?

at gøre det forbi.explanation: "At gøre det forbi" means "to end it", about a relationship: Han gjorde det forbi med hende (He ended it with her). A common everyday way to say it is at slå op (to break up).

sentence.da: Hun elsker ham ikke mere og vil **gøre det forbi**.
sentence.en: She no longer loves him and wants to end it.

at gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden.explanation: "At gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden" means "to make a virtue of necessity": to do what you must do anyway and present it as a good choice of your own. People say it when someone has no choice but acts proud of it.

forms.da: Han gør en dyd af nødvendigheden
forms.en: He makes a virtue of necessity

forms.da: Hun gjorde en dyd af nødvendigheden
forms.en: She made a virtue of necessity

forms.da: Vi må gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden
forms.en: We have to make a virtue of necessity

related.da: at gøre det bedste ud af det
related.en: to make the best of it

related.da: at gøre gode miner til slet spil
related.en: to put on a brave face

related.da: at bide i det sure æble

sentence.da: Vi har ikke råd til ferie og må **gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden**.
sentence.en: We cannot afford a vacation and must make a virtue of necessity.

at gøre en forskel.explanation: "At gøre en forskel" means "to make a difference": Din hjælp gør en forskel (Your help makes a difference). To say how big, add a word: at gøre en stor forskel (to make a big difference).

sentence.da: Et smil kan **gøre en forskel** for en ensom person.
sentence.en: A smile can make a difference for a lonely person.

at gøre færdig.explanation: "At gøre færdig" means "to finish" something: Jeg gør opgaven færdig (I am finishing the assignment). To say you are done yourself, use at blive færdig: Jeg bliver færdig klokken fem (I will be done at five).

sentence.da: Lad mig lige **gøre færdig**, og så kommer jeg.
sentence.en: Let me just finish, and then I will come.

at gøre grin med.explanation: "At gøre grin med" means "to make fun of" someone: Hun gør grin med mig (She makes fun of me). The person or thing you laugh at comes after med (with).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **gøre grin med** andre.
sentence.en: You should not make fun of others.

at gøre indtryk.explanation: "At gøre indtryk" means "to make an impression", to affect someone strongly so that they remember it. The person affected comes after på (on): Filmen gjorde stort indtryk på mig (The film made a big impression on me).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **gøre indtryk** på sine nye kolleger.
sentence.en: He wants to make an impression on his new colleagues.

at gøre klar.explanation: "At gøre klar" means "to get something ready": Jeg gør maden klar (I am getting the food ready). To get yourself ready, add mig: Jeg gør mig klar (I am getting myself ready).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **gøre klar** til festen.
sentence.en: I have to get ready for the party.

at gøre noget ved.explanation: "At gøre noget ved" means "to do something about" a problem: Vi må gøre noget ved støjen (We have to do something about the noise). Said alone, Gør noget! means "Do something!".

sentence.da: Vi må **gøre noget ved** det nu.
sentence.en: We have to do something about it now.

at gøre ondt.explanation: "At gøre ondt" means "to hurt". The part that hurts comes first: Min fod gør ondt (My foot hurts). You can also say Jeg har ondt i foden (I have a pain in the foot).

sentence.da: Det kan **gøre ondt** at falde på isen.
sentence.en: It can hurt to fall on the ice.

at gøre rent.explanation: "At gøre rent" means "to clean" a place. It is built from gøre (to do) and rent (clean), so it literally means to make clean. The place can go in the middle: Jeg gør køkkenet rent (I clean the kitchen).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gøre rent** i huset.
sentence.en: We have to clean the house.

at gøre sig umage.explanation: "At gøre sig umage" means "to make an effort", to put real work into doing something well. Sig changes with the person: Jeg gør mig umage (I make an effort), Du gør dig umage (You make an effort).

sentence.da: Eleverne vil **gøre sig umage** med opgaven.
sentence.en: The students will make an effort with the assignment.

at gøre sit bedste.explanation: "At gøre sit bedste" means "to do one's best". Sit (one's) changes with who does it: Han gør sit bedste (He does his best), Jeg gør mit bedste (I do my best).

sentence.da: Hver elev skal **gøre sit bedste** til prøven.
sentence.en: Each student must do their best for the test.

en gaben.explanation: "En gaben" means "a yawn", the long, deep breath with an open mouth when you are tired. The word is also used without en for yawning in general: Gaben smitter (Yawning is contagious).

sentence.da: Han skjulte sin **gaben** bag hånden.
sentence.en: He hid his yawn behind his hand.

en gade.explanation: "En gade" means "a street". For a bigger road, for example between towns, use en vej (a road).

sentence.da: Vi går ned ad en **gade** med huse.
sentence.en: We walk down a street with houses.

en gadedør.explanation: "En gadedør" means "a street door", the main door of a building that opens onto the street. It is built from gade (street) and dør (door). Dør also means "dies", as in Fuglen dør (The bird dies).

sentence.da: Huset har en blå **gadedør** ud til gaden.
sentence.en: The house has a blue street door facing the street.

en gadekat.explanation: "En gadekat" means "a stray cat", a cat with no home. It is built from gade (street) and kat (cat). A cat that lives with a family is en huskat (a house cat).

sentence.da: En **gadekat** bor ude og har ingen ejer.
sentence.en: A stray cat lives outside and has no owner.

en gadelygte.explanation: "En gadelygte" means "a streetlight". It is built from gade (street) and lygte (light), and gade also starts en gadekat (a stray cat).

sentence.da: Om natten lyser en **gadelygte** gaden op.
sentence.en: At night, a streetlight lights up the street.

en gaffel.explanation: "En gaffel" means "a fork", the pointed tool you use to pick up food. It is paired with a knife in the set phrase kniv og gaffel (knife and fork).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser maden med en **gaffel**.
sentence.en: I eat the food with a fork.

en galakse.explanation: "En galakse" means "a galaxy", a huge group of billions of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity.

sentence.da: Vores sol ligger i en **galakse**, som hedder Mælkevejen.
sentence.en: Our sun lies in a galaxy called the Milky Way.

en gallerist.explanation: "En gallerist" means "a gallery owner", someone who runs a place that shows and sells paintings and sculpture. A gallerist often chooses which painters to show and helps them find buyers.

sentence.da: Hun er **gallerist** og sælger malerier for unge kunstnere.
sentence.en: She is a gallery owner and sells paintings for young artists.

en galning.explanation: "En galning" means "a madman", a person who does wild or dangerous things. It sounds harsh when you are angry, but friends use it to tease: Din galning! (You lunatic!)

sentence.da: Kun en **galning** kører hundrede kilometer i timen i byen.
sentence.en: Only a madman drives a hundred kilometers an hour in town.

en gang.explanation: "En gang" means "a hallway", the passage inside a building that leads to the rooms. The same word also means "a time": to gange (twice).

sentence.da: Der er mange døre i den lange **gang**.
sentence.en: There are many doors in the long hallway.

en gang imellem.explanation: "En gang imellem" means "once in a while", for things that do not happen often. It is less often than tit (often) but more often than aldrig (never).

forms.da: Jeg ser dem en gang imellem.
forms.en: I see them once in a while.
once in a while in the summer

forms.da: Vi spiser ude en gang imellem.
forms.en: We eat out once in a while.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser pizza **en gang imellem**.
sentence.en: I eat pizza once in a while.

en gang om ugen.explanation: "En gang om ugen" means "once a week". Change the number to say how often: tre gange om ugen (three times a week). Change the last word to change the time: en gang om dagen (once a day).

sentence.da: Jeg træner **en gang om ugen**.
sentence.en: I work out once a week.

en garage.explanation: "En garage" means "a garage", where you park a car.

sentence.da: Vi har en **garage** til bilen.
sentence.en: We have a garage for the car.

en garanti.explanation: "En garanti" means "a warranty", the maker's promise to fix a product. It also means "a guarantee" in general: Jeg giver dig min garanti (I give you my guarantee).

sentence.da: Der er to års **garanti** på computeren.
sentence.en: The computer has a two-year warranty.

en gartner.explanation: "En gartner" means "a gardener", someone who works with plants and flowers as a job. The workplace is et gartneri (a plant nursery).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **gartner** og passer planter i parken.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a gardener and takes care of plants in the park.

en gate.explanation: "En gate" means "a gate" at an airport, where you board your plane. A garden gate is en låge (a gate).

sentence.da: Flyet til Rom går fra **gate** tolv.
sentence.en: The plane to Rome leaves from gate twelve.

en gaveindpakning.explanation: "En gaveindpakning" means "a gift wrapping", the paper and ribbon around a present, or the wrapping service in a shop: Kan jeg få den gaveindpakket? (Can I get it gift wrapped?)

sentence.da: Butikken tilbyder gratis **gaveindpakning**.
sentence.en: The shop offers free gift wrapping.

en ged.explanation: "En ged" means "a goat", a farm animal with horns. Goat cheese is called gedeost.

sentence.da: En **ged** spiser græs og giver mælk.
sentence.en: A goat eats grass and gives milk.

en gedde.explanation: "En gedde" means "a pike", a long freshwater fish with a flat snout. It is common in Danish lakes and rivers and a favorite catch for anglers.

sentence.da: En **gedde** er en rovfisk med skarpe tænder i søen.
sentence.en: A pike is a predatory fish with sharp teeth in the lake.

en genbrugsbutik.explanation: "En genbrugsbutik" means "a secondhand shop", a store that sells clothes and things that other people owned before.

sentence.da: I en **genbrugsbutik** er tøjet brugt og billigt.
sentence.en: In a secondhand shop the clothes are used and cheap.

en genbrugsstation.explanation: "En genbrugsstation" means "a recycling center", where you leave bigger things you no longer need, like old furniture or branches.

sentence.da: Man sorterer sit affald på en **genbrugsstation**.
sentence.en: You sort your waste at a recycling center.

en general.explanation: "En general" means "a general", a senior army commander. The navy has en admiral (an admiral) at the same level.

sentence.da: En **general** er den højeste officer i hæren.
sentence.en: A general is the highest officer in the army.

en generation.explanation: "En generation" means "a generation", all the people born at about the same time. It also counts the steps in a family: tre generationer (three generations) can be grandparents, parents and children.

sentence.da: Børn og deres forældre er ikke af samme **generation**.
sentence.en: Children and their parents are not of the same generation.

en generationskløft.explanation: "En generationskløft" means "a generation gap", when older and younger people have very different views and habits. Kløft is also a real ravine in the mountains, so the word pictures a deep gap between two groups.

sentence.da: Der er en stor **generationskløft** mellem mine bedsteforældre og mig.
sentence.en: There is a big generation gap between my grandparents and me.

en gennemgang.explanation: "En gennemgang" means "a review" or "a walkthrough", looking at something step by step, like a text or a plan. On a sign, Gennemgang forbudt means "No way through", because the word can also mean a path you walk through.

sentence.da: Læreren laver en **gennemgang** af reglerne, før prøven starter.
sentence.en: The teacher goes over the rules before the test starts.

en gennemsnitsløn.explanation: "En gennemsnitsløn" means "an average salary", the typical pay across a group of people. A few very high salaries pull it up, so it can be higher than what most people earn.

sentence.da: En **gennemsnitsløn** er summen af alle lønninger delt med antallet af personer.
sentence.en: An average salary is the sum of all salaries divided by the number of people.

en genopretning.explanation: "En genopretning" means "a recovery", putting something that has broken down back in working order, such as an economy or public order. For a person who gets well after illness, Danes say at komme sig (to get better) instead.

sentence.da: Regeringen arbejder på en **genopretning** af landets økonomi.
sentence.en: The government is working on a recovery of the country's economy.

en genre.explanation: "En genre" means "a genre", a type of music, film or book.

sentence.da: Rock er en **genre** inden for musik.
sentence.en: Rock is a genre within music.

en genstand.explanation: "En genstand" means "an object", a physical item you can point to. Everyday speech uses en ting (a thing): Hvad er det for en ting? (What is that thing?). A report says en ukendt genstand (an unidentified object).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en mærkelig **genstand** i haven.
sentence.en: The police found a strange object in the garden.

en genstart.explanation: "En genstart" means "a restart", when you shut a device down and start it again, such as a computer or a phone. The prefix gen- means "again", as in at genbruge (to reuse).

sentence.da: Hvis telefonen hænger, kan en **genstart** ofte løse problemet.
sentence.en: If the phone freezes, a restart can often solve the problem.

en genvej.explanation: "En genvej" means "a shortcut", a quicker way to get somewhere. It is also used on computers: en tastaturgenvej (a keyboard shortcut).

sentence.da: Vi tog en **genvej** og kom hurtigt hjem.
sentence.en: We took a shortcut and got home quickly.

en gerning.explanation: "En gerning" means "a deed", something a person does that is seen as important, good or bad. It is common in the pair ord og gerning (word and deed): Hun hjælper både i ord og gerning (She helps in both word and deed).

sentence.da: En god **gerning** er noget, man gør for at hjælpe andre.
sentence.en: A good deed is something you do to help others.

en gerningsmand.explanation: "En gerningsmand" means "a perpetrator", the person who carried out a crime. You mostly meet it in news and police reports. When nobody knows whether it was a man or a woman, police can say en gerningsperson (a culprit).

sentence.da: Politiet har fundet den **gerningsmand**, der brød ind i butikken.
sentence.en: The police have found the perpetrator who broke into the store.

en gestus.explanation: "En gestus" means "a gesture", a small act that shows a feeling or an intention, such as kindness. For a movement of the hand, Danes more often say en håndbevægelse (a hand movement).

sentence.da: Det var en pæn **gestus**, at han bød os på kaffe.
sentence.en: It was a nice gesture that he offered us coffee.

en gevinst.explanation: "En gevinst" means "a prize" or "winnings", the money or thing you receive from a lottery or a game. It also means a gain: Det er en gevinst for alle (It is a gain for everyone).

sentence.da: Hun brugte sin **gevinst** fra lotteriet på en rejse.
sentence.en: She spent her prize from the lottery on a trip.

en gift.explanation: "En gift" means "a poison", something that can make you very sick. The same spelling also means "married": Han er gift (He is married).

sentence.da: Slangen har en stærk **gift**.
sentence.en: The snake has a strong poison.

en giraf.explanation: "En giraf" means "a giraffe", the tallest animal on land, found in Africa.

sentence.da: En **giraf** har en meget lang hals.
sentence.en: A giraffe has a very long neck.

en gletsjer.explanation: "En gletsjer" means "a glacier", a huge mass of ice formed from packed snow that builds up over many years on land.

sentence.da: En **gletsjer** flytter sig langsomt ned ad bjerget.
sentence.en: A glacier moves slowly down the mountain.

en globus.explanation: "En globus" means "a globe", a round model of the Earth. A flat picture of the world is et kort (a map).

sentence.da: På en **globus** ser man hele jorden.
sentence.en: On a globe you see the whole Earth.

en gnist.explanation: "En gnist" means "a spark", a tiny bright flash that flies from a fire or from electricity. It is also used for a small beginning of a feeling: en gnist af håb (a spark of hope).

sentence.da: Når man slår to sten mod hinanden, kan der komme en **gnist**.
sentence.en: When you strike two stones together, a spark can appear.

en godkendelse.explanation: "En godkendelse" means "an approval", an official yes from someone who decides, like a boss or an authority. It comes from at godkende (to approve).

sentence.da: Før butikken åbner, skal den have en **godkendelse** fra kommunen.
sentence.en: Before the shop opens, it must have an approval from the municipality.

en godtgørelse.explanation: "En godtgørelse" means "a reimbursement", money paid back to you to cover costs you had. It is common with work: kørselsgodtgørelse (mileage allowance) is what you get when you use your own car for your job.

sentence.da: Jeg får **godtgørelse** for benzinen, når jeg kører for arbejdet.
sentence.en: I get reimbursement for the gas when I drive for work.

en gorilla.explanation: "En gorilla" means "a gorilla", a big, strong animal that lives in the forests of Africa.

sentence.da: Den store **gorilla** spiser blade og frugt.
sentence.en: The big gorilla eats leaves and fruit.

en grad.explanation: "En grad" means "a degree", for temperature, angles and university studies: Vandet fryser ved nul grader (Water freezes at zero degrees). Hun har en grad fra universitetet (She has a degree from the university).

sentence.da: Det er kun én **grad** ude i dag.
sentence.en: It is only one degree outside today.

en graf.explanation: "En graf" means "a graph", a picture of numbers drawn as a line, a curve or bars, so you can see change at a glance.

sentence.da: På en **graf** kan man se, hvordan prisen stiger hver måned.
sentence.en: On a graph you can see how the price rises every month.

en grammatik.explanation: "En grammatik" means "a grammar", the system for how words fit together in speech and writing.

sentence.da: Jeg øver reglerne i dansk **grammatik**.
sentence.en: I practice the rules of Danish grammar.

en gran.explanation: "En gran" means "a spruce" or "a fir", an evergreen tree with cones, common in Danish forests. Many Danes use en nordmannsgran (a Nordmann fir) as a Christmas tree.

sentence.da: En **gran** har nåle og er grøn hele vinteren.
sentence.en: A spruce has needles and is green all winter.

en granat.explanation: "En granat" means "a grenade", a small explosive weapon that is thrown by hand or fired from a gun and bursts into pieces. The fruit is not a granat but et granatæble (a pomegranate).

sentence.da: En **granat** eksploderer kort efter, at splitten er trukket ud.
sentence.en: A grenade explodes shortly after the pin is pulled out.

en gratisavis.explanation: "En gratisavis" means "a free newspaper", one that is handed out or put in your mailbox, often with local news and shop offers.

sentence.da: En **gratisavis** koster ingenting, fordi reklamerne betaler for den.
sentence.en: A free newspaper costs nothing because the ads pay for it.

en grav.explanation: "En grav" means "a grave", the place where a dead person is buried. It is also a long ditch dug in the ground, as in en voldgrav (a moat).

sentence.da: Efter begravelsen ligger den døde i en **grav** på kirkegården.
sentence.en: After the funeral the dead person lies in a grave in the cemetery.

en graviditet.explanation: "En graviditet" means "a pregnancy", the time when a woman is expecting a baby. It lasts about nine months and is built from gravid (pregnant).

sentence.da: Under en **graviditet** vokser barnet i moderens mave.
sentence.en: During a pregnancy the baby grows in the mother's belly.

en graviditetstest.explanation: "En graviditetstest" means "a pregnancy test", a small kit that shows with a line or a sign whether a woman is expecting a baby. Many people use it at home.

sentence.da: Med en **graviditetstest** kan man selv se, om man er gravid.
sentence.en: With a pregnancy test you can see for yourself whether you are pregnant.

en gravko.explanation: "En gravko" means "an excavator", a big machine that digs holes. It is built on at grave (to dig), which also gives en grav (a grave).

sentence.da: En **gravko** graver et stort hul.
sentence.en: An excavator digs a big hole.

en gravsten.explanation: "En gravsten" means "a gravestone", a stone that marks where someone is buried. It is built from grav (a grave) and sten (a stone).

sentence.da: På en **gravsten** står den dødes navn og fødselsår.
sentence.en: On a gravestone you find the dead person's name and birth year.

en gren.explanation: "En gren" means "a branch", the woody part that grows out sideways from a tree.

sentence.da: Fuglen sidder på en **gren** i træet.
sentence.en: The bird sits on a branch in the tree.

en grill.explanation: "En grill" means "a grill" or "a barbecue", for cooking outside. The matching verb is at grille (to grill): Vi griller pølser (We grill sausages).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad ude på en **grill**.
sentence.en: We cook outside on a grill.

en grillbar.explanation: "En grillbar" means "a grill bar", a simple, cheap takeaway place, often open late and with only a few tables.

sentence.da: På en **grillbar** kan man købe burgere og pølser med pommes frites.
sentence.en: At a grill bar you can buy burgers and sausages with fries.

en grillfest.explanation: "En grillfest" means "a barbecue party". It is built from en grill (a grill) and en fest (a party). The verb at grille (to grill) is how you say you are barbecuing: Vi griller i aften (We are barbecuing tonight).

sentence.da: Til en **grillfest** spiser vi pølser og salat.
sentence.en: At a barbecue party we eat sausages and salad.

en grimasse.explanation: "En grimasse" means "a grimace", a twisted face you make from pain or a bad taste, or on purpose to be funny. Danes say at skære grimasser (to pull faces), using skære, which normally means "to cut".

sentence.da: Han lavede en **grimasse**, fordi citronen var meget sur.
sentence.en: He made a grimace because the lemon was very sour.

en gris.explanation: "En gris" means "a pig". Du er en gris! (You are a pig!) is an insult, so keep the word for the animal. Pork is svinekød, built from et svin (a swine), another word for pig.

sentence.da: Jeg ser en lyserød **gris** på gården.
sentence.en: I see a pink pig on the farm.

en grund.explanation: "En grund" means "a reason". Af den grund means "for that reason". It can also mean a plot of land that you build on: Vi køber en grund og bygger et hus (We buy a plot of land and build a house).

sentence.da: Der er ingen **grund** til at være bange.
sentence.en: There is no reason to be afraid.

en grundlov.explanation: "En grundlov" means "a constitution", the highest law of a country, which sets out how it is run and what freedoms people have. It is built from grund (base) and lov (law).

sentence.da: I en **grundlov** står der, hvilke rettigheder borgerne har.
sentence.en: A constitution states which rights the citizens have.

en grundskole.explanation: "En grundskole" means "a primary school". In Denmark it covers the whole stretch from about age 6 to 16 (grades 0 to 9), not just the first years.

sentence.da: Danske børn går i **grundskole** i ti år.
sentence.en: Danish children attend primary school for ten years.

en gruppe.explanation: "En gruppe" means "a group" of people or things. Danish has no word for "of" here: en gruppe børn (a group of children).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder i en **gruppe** på fire.
sentence.en: We work in a group of four.

en gryde.explanation: "En gryde" means "a pot", for cooking soup, pasta or rice on the stove. For frying you use en pande (a pan) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg koger kartofler i en stor **gryde**.
sentence.en: I boil potatoes in a big pot.

en grydelap.explanation: "En grydelap" means "a pot holder", a thick cloth for holding hot things.

sentence.da: Jeg tager brødet ud af ovnen med en **grydelap**.
sentence.en: I take the bread out of the oven with a pot holder.

en grænse.explanation: "En grænse" means "a border", for example between two countries. It also means a limit: Alt har en grænse (Everything has a limit).

sentence.da: Ved en **grænse** skal du vise dit pas.
sentence.en: At a border you must show your passport.

en grænseværdi.explanation: "En grænseværdi" means "a limit value", a number set by law or rules that must not be passed, for example for chemicals in food or drinking water. It is built from grænse (limit) and værdi (value).

sentence.da: Der er en **grænseværdi** for, hvor meget støj en fabrik må lave.
sentence.en: There is a limit value for how much noise a factory may make.

en græshoppe.explanation: "En græshoppe" means "a grasshopper", a small jumping insect, often green, with six legs. Many kinds make a chirping sound.

sentence.da: En **græshoppe** kan hoppe langt, fordi dens bagben er stærke.
sentence.en: A grasshopper can jump far because its back legs are strong.

en græsslåmaskine.explanation: "En græsslåmaskine" means "a lawnmower". It is built from græs (grass), at slå (to mow) and en maskine (a machine). Slå also means to hit, so at slå græs (to mow grass) is literally to hit grass.

sentence.da: Græsset er højt, og jeg henter min **græsslåmaskine**.
sentence.en: The grass is tall, and I am getting my lawnmower.

en græsslåning.explanation: "En græsslåning" means "a lawn mowing", the job of cutting the grass. Slå normally means "to hit", but Danes use it in at slå græs (to mow the lawn).

sentence.da: Efter en times **græsslåning** er plænen pæn og kort.
sentence.en: After an hour of lawn mowing, the lawn is neat and short.

en grævling.explanation: "En grævling" means "a badger", a stocky gray animal with a white stripe on its face. It lives in forests, comes out at night and is rarely seen.

sentence.da: En **grævling** bor i et hul i skoven og sover om dagen.
sentence.en: A badger lives in a hole in the forest and sleeps during the day.

en grønlænder.explanation: "En grønlænder" means "a Greenlander", a person from Greenland. The Danish name of the country is Grønland, and the language is grønlandsk (Greenlandic).

sentence.da: En **grønlænder** kommer fra Grønland og taler grønlandsk.
sentence.en: A Greenlander comes from Greenland and speaks Greenlandic.

en grønthandler.explanation: "En grønthandler" means "a greengrocer", someone who sells fresh fruit and vegetables. It is also the shop itself, so Danes can say Jeg går hen til grønthandleren (I am going over to the greengrocer's).

sentence.da: Jeg køber æbler og gulerødder hos en **grønthandler**.
sentence.en: I buy apples and carrots at a greengrocer's.

en grøntsag.explanation: "En grøntsag" means "a vegetable". It is built from grøn (green) and sag (thing), so it is literally a green thing. Sag is a common word for a matter or a case, as in en retssag (a court case).

sentence.da: En gulerod er en **grøntsag**.
sentence.en: A carrot is a vegetable.

en gud.explanation: "En gud" means "a god", one of many gods. For the one God, say Gud without en: Tror du på Gud? (Do you believe in God?).

sentence.da: Thor var en **gud** i gamle dage.
sentence.en: Thor was a god in the old days.

en gudfar.explanation: "En gudfar" means "a godfather", a man chosen by the parents to be a special adult in a child's life, often at the christening.

sentence.da: Min **gudfar** er min fars bedste ven.
sentence.en: My godfather is my dad's best friend.

en gudmor.explanation: "En gudmor" means "a godmother", a woman chosen by the parents to be a special adult in a child's life, often at the christening.

sentence.da: Min **gudmor** er min mors bedste veninde.
sentence.en: My godmother is my mom's best friend.

en guide.explanation: "En guide" means "a guide", a person who shows visitors around a place.

sentence.da: Vores **guide** viser os den gamle by.
sentence.en: Our guide shows us the old town.

en guidebog.explanation: "En guidebog" means "a guidebook", a book with sights and tips for a trip. It is built from guide and bog (book). Guide also means a person who shows tourists around: En guide viser os byen (A guide shows us the town).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **guidebog** før turen.
sentence.en: I read a guidebook before the trip.

en guirlande.explanation: "En guirlande" means "a garland", a long decorative string of flowers, leaves or small flags that is hung up for parties and holidays. You often hang one along a wall or over a door.

sentence.da: Til festen hænger der en **guirlande** af papir over bordet.
sentence.en: For the party there is a paper garland hanging over the table.

en guitar.explanation: "En guitar" means "a guitar". With at spille (to play), Danish leaves out the word for "the": Jeg spiller guitar means "I play the guitar".

sentence.da: Min bror spiller **guitar** i et band.
sentence.en: My brother plays guitar in a band.

en guldfisk.explanation: "En guldfisk" means "a goldfish", an orange pet fish that lives in a bowl.

sentence.da: Der svømmer en **guldfisk** rundt i en skål.
sentence.en: A goldfish is swimming around in a bowl.

en guldsmed.explanation: "En guldsmed" means "a dragonfly", the insect with a long thin body that you see over lakes in summer. The same word also means a goldsmith, someone who makes jewelry from gold: Ringen er lavet af en guldsmed (The ring was made by a goldsmith).

sentence.da: Over søen flyver en **guldsmed** med gennemsigtige vinger.
sentence.en: Over the lake flies a dragonfly with transparent wings.

en gulerod.explanation: "En gulerod" means "a carrot". It is built from gul (yellow) and rod (root), so it is literally a yellow root. The name says yellow, though carrots are orange.

sentence.da: Kaninen spiser en orange **gulerod**.
sentence.en: The rabbit eats an orange carrot.

en gulvvask.explanation: "En gulvvask" means "a floor washing", the job of cleaning floors with water. It is built from gulv (floor) and vask (washing), and it describes the same job as at vaske gulv (to wash the floor).

sentence.da: En **gulvvask** med varmt vand og sæbe tager kun ti minutter.
sentence.en: A floor washing with hot water and soap takes only ten minutes.

en gummistøvle.explanation: "En gummistøvle" means "a rubber boot", the waterproof boot for rain and mud. Most often you say it in pairs: et par gummistøvler (a pair of rubber boots).

sentence.da: Han mistede en **gummistøvle** i mudderet.
sentence.en: He lost a rubber boot in the mud.

en gut.explanation: "En gut" means "a guy" or "a lad", an informal word for a young male. Friends use it when they talk to each other: Hej, gutter! (Hi, guys!).

sentence.da: Han er en flink **gut**, som altid hjælper sine venner.
sentence.en: He is a nice lad who always helps his friends.

en guvernør.explanation: "En guvernør" means "a governor", the head of a state in the USA, or of a region in some other countries.

sentence.da: En **guvernør** leder en amerikansk delstat.
sentence.en: A governor leads an American state.

en gyde.explanation: "En gyde" means "an alley", a very narrow lane between buildings. It is narrower than a normal road, and you often find alleys in old town centers.

sentence.da: Den smalle **gyde** mellem husene er næsten mørk.
sentence.en: The narrow alley between the houses is almost dark.

en gymnastiksal.explanation: "En gymnastiksal" means "a school gym", the big hall where PE lessons are held. It is built from gymnastik (gymnastics) and sal (hall).

sentence.da: Børnene har idræt i skolens **gymnastiksal**, når det regner.
sentence.en: The children have PE in the school gym when it rains.

en gynge.explanation: "En gynge" means "a swing", the kind at a playground. The action is at gynge (to swing, to rock): Barnet gynger (The child is swinging).

sentence.da: Far skubber mig på en **gynge**.
sentence.en: Dad pushes me on a swing.

en gåde.explanation: "En gåde" means "a riddle / mystery", a short question that is hard to answer and has to be worked out. It also means anything strange that nobody can explain: Det er en gåde, hvorfor hun forsvandt (It is a mystery why she disappeared).

sentence.da: Børnene prøver at løse en **gåde** i bogen.
sentence.en: The children try to solve a riddle in the book.

en gågade.explanation: "En gågade" means "a pedestrian street", a street with no cars. It is built from gå (walk) and gade (street). Gade also appears in other street words, such as en sidegade (a side street).

sentence.da: Ingen biler må køre i en **gågade**.
sentence.en: Cars may not drive in a pedestrian street.

en gård.explanation: "En gård" means "a farm" and also "a courtyard". In the country it is a farm. In a city, gården is the shared yard behind an apartment building.

sentence.da: Vi besøger en **gård** og ser køer og grise.
sentence.en: We visit a farm and see cows and pigs.

en gårdhave.explanation: "En gårdhave" means "a courtyard garden", a small garden inside a block of buildings. It is built from gård (courtyard) and have (garden). Gård also means a farm: Vi bor på en gård (We live on a farm).

sentence.da: Der er en lille **gårdhave** med blomster bag huset.
sentence.en: There is a small courtyard garden with flowers behind the house.

en gås.explanation: "En gås" means "a goose", a big bird with a long neck that flies in groups. The meat is also eaten: gåsesteg (roast goose).

sentence.da: En **gås** er en stor fugl og bor ved vandet.
sentence.en: A goose is a big bird and lives by the water.

en gåtur.explanation: "En gåtur" means "a walk". It is built from gå (walk) and tur (trip). You say at gå en tur or at tage på gåtur, both meaning "to go for a walk".

sentence.da: Vi tager på **gåtur** i skoven.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in the forest.

en gæld.explanation: "En gæld" means "a debt", money you owe to a person or a bank. It is mostly used without en: Hun har ingen gæld (She has no debt).

sentence.da: Efter huskøbet har de **gæld** til banken.
sentence.en: After buying the house, they have debt to the bank.

en gæst.explanation: "En gæst" means "a guest", for visitors in your home and also for hotel guests: Vi får gæster (We are having guests).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad til vores **gæst**.
sentence.en: We cook for our guest.

en gætteleg.explanation: "En gætteleg" means "a guessing game". It is built from at gætte (to guess) and leg (game). Leg also gives at lege (to play): Børnene leger udenfor (The children are playing outside).

sentence.da: I en **gætteleg** skal du gætte svaret.
sentence.en: In a guessing game, you have to guess the answer.

et gab.explanation: "Et gab" means "a yawn", the wide open mouth you make when you are tired or bored. The same word also names the wide open mouth of a big animal, such as a lion's.

sentence.da: Han skjuler et **gab** bag hånden, fordi mødet er så langt.
sentence.en: He hides a yawn behind his hand because the meeting is so long.

et gadekryds.explanation: "Et gadekryds" means "an intersection", where two streets cross. It is built from en gade (a street) and et kryds (a cross). Kryds also means a cross mark: Sæt et kryds her (Put a cross here).

sentence.da: Drej til højre ved næste **gadekryds**.
sentence.en: Turn right at the next intersection.

et galleri.explanation: "Et galleri" means "a gallery", a place that shows art, often for sale.

sentence.da: Vi ser på kunst i et lille **galleri**.
sentence.en: We look at art in a small gallery.

et gardin.explanation: "Et gardin" means "a curtain", hung at a window. To close it, say trække for (draw): Hun trækker gardinerne for (She draws the curtains).

sentence.da: Et **gardin** hænger foran vinduet og holder lyset ude.
sentence.en: A curtain hangs in front of the window and keeps the light out.

et gavekort.explanation: "Et gavekort" means "a gift card", a card with money on it that you give as a present. It is made of en gave (a gift) and et kort (a card).

sentence.da: Med et **gavekort** kan man købe ting.
sentence.en: With a gift card you can buy things.

et gear.explanation: "Et gear" means "a gear", on a car or a bike: Jeg kører i andet gear (I am driving in second gear).

sentence.da: Jeg skifter **gear**, når vejen går opad.
sentence.en: I shift gears when the road goes uphill.

et gebyr.explanation: "Et gebyr" means "a fee", an amount you pay to a bank, an authority or a company for a service, or for being late: et rykkergebyr (a reminder fee).

sentence.da: Banken tager et **gebyr** på halvtreds kroner for hver overførsel.
sentence.en: The bank charges a fee of fifty kroner for each transfer.

et gen.explanation: "Et gen" means "a gene", a tiny unit inside the body that carries instructions passed from parents to children, for example for eye color. Danes also say Det ligger i generne (It runs in the family), literally in the genes.

sentence.da: Hvert **gen** bærer instruktioner om, hvordan kroppen skal bygges.
sentence.en: Each gene carries instructions about how the body is built.

et geni.explanation: "Et geni" means "a genius", a person with a brilliant mind. To say what someone is brilliant at, use i or til: Hun er et geni i matematik (She is a genius at math).

sentence.da: Min bror er et **geni** til matematik.
sentence.en: My brother is a genius at math.

et gennembrud.explanation: "Et gennembrud" means "a breakthrough", a big step forward that comes after a long period of effort, in science, sport or a career. For an artist, it is the moment they become well known: Hendes gennembrud kom i 2010 (Her breakthrough came in 2010).

sentence.da: Efter mange års arbejde fik forskerne endelig et **gennembrud**.
sentence.en: After many years of work, the researchers finally got a breakthrough.

et gennemsnit.explanation: "Et gennemsnit" means "an average", the number you get by adding several numbers and dividing by how many there are. With i, it means "on average": i gennemsnit.

sentence.da: Jeg sover syv timer i **gennemsnit**.
sentence.en: I sleep seven hours on average.

et gerningssted.explanation: "Et gerningssted" means "a crime scene", the place where a crime happened. The police close it off with tape and search it carefully, so nobody disturbs the evidence.

sentence.da: Det sted, hvor en forbrydelse er sket, kaldes et **gerningssted**.
sentence.en: The place where a crime has happened is called a crime scene.

et gevir.explanation: "Et gevir" means "a set of antlers", the branched growth on the head of a stag. The word covers the whole set at once, so one animal has one gevir.

sentence.da: Hjorten har et stort **gevir** med mange spidser.
sentence.en: The deer has a large set of antlers with many points.

et gevær.explanation: "Et gevær" means "a rifle", a long gun that you hold against your shoulder when you fire it, used for hunting and by soldiers. A small gun held in one hand is called en pistol.

sentence.da: Jægeren sigter omhyggeligt, før han skyder med sit **gevær**.
sentence.en: The hunter aims carefully before he shoots with his rifle.

et gidsel.explanation: "Et gidsel" means "a hostage", a person who is held by someone who wants something in return. You say tage nogen som gidsel (take someone hostage).

sentence.da: Bankrøveren holder et **gidsel**, og politiet forhandler med ham.
sentence.en: The bank robber is holding a hostage, and the police are negotiating with him.

et glas.explanation: "Et glas" means "a glass", both the material and a drinking glass. Danish has no word for of here: et glas vand (a glass of water) and et glas vin (a glass of wine).

sentence.da: Man drikker vand af et **glas**.
sentence.en: You drink water from a glass.

et glimt.explanation: "Et glimt" means "a glimpse" and "a gleam": a very short sight of something, or a brief flash of light. A playful look is et glimt i øjet (a twinkle in the eye).

sentence.da: Hun fik et **glimt** af solen mellem skyerne.
sentence.en: She got a glimpse of the sun between the clouds.

et gram.explanation: "Et gram" means "a gram", a unit of weight used for small amounts, such as flour or spices.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge to hundrede **gram** mel.
sentence.en: I need two hundred grams of flour.

et grin.explanation: "Et grin" means "a laugh" and also "a grin". For a smile, say et smil.

sentence.da: Vi fik et godt **grin** sammen i går.
sentence.en: We had a good laugh together yesterday.

et grundlag.explanation: "Et grundlag" means "a basis", the base that something rests on, such as a decision, a law or an argument. A common pairing is et solidt grundlag (a solid basis).

sentence.da: Aftalen blev det **grundlag**, som resten af planen byggede på.
sentence.en: The agreement became the basis that the rest of the plan was built on.

et grundstof.explanation: "Et grundstof" means "a chemical element", a pure material that chemistry cannot break down into anything simpler, such as ilt (oxygen) or jern (iron). All other materials are made by combining these.

sentence.da: Guld er et **grundstof**, som ikke kan deles i noget enklere.
sentence.en: Gold is an element that cannot be split into anything simpler.

et gudbarn.explanation: "Et gudbarn" means "a godchild", a child you are a godparent to.

sentence.da: Mit **gudbarn** fylder fem år i dag.
sentence.en: My godchild turns five today.

et guldbryllup.explanation: "Et guldbryllup" means "a golden wedding anniversary", the celebration of 50 years of marriage. The word is only for the anniversary party: the day of the wedding itself is et bryllup (a wedding).

sentence.da: Mine bedsteforældre har været gift i halvtreds år og holder **guldbryllup**.
sentence.en: My grandparents have been married for fifty years and are celebrating their golden wedding.

et gulv.explanation: "Et gulv" means "a floor", the surface you walk on in a room. For a level of a building, use en etage (a story): anden etage (second floor).

sentence.da: Et **gulv** er lavet af træ eller sten.
sentence.en: A floor is made of wood or stone.

et gulvtæppe.explanation: "Et gulvtæppe" means "a carpet". Gulv (floor) shows that it lies on the floor, since et tæppe alone can also be a blanket.

sentence.da: Vi har et blødt **gulvtæppe** i stuen.
sentence.en: We have a soft carpet in the living room.

et gymnasium.explanation: "Et gymnasium" means "a high school", the three years at about age 16 to 19 that prepare you for further study: Min datter går på gymnasiet (My daughter goes to high school). Do not mix it up with English "gym": a sports hall is en idrætshal.

sentence.da: Efter folkeskolen går mange unge på et **gymnasium**.
sentence.en: After primary school, many young people go to a gymnasium.

et gys.explanation: "Et gys" means "a shudder", a quick shiver through the body, caused by cold, fear or disgust. Det gav mig et gys (It gave me a shudder) says that something scared or disgusted you.

sentence.da: Et **gys** løb ned ad ryggen på mig, da døren gik op.
sentence.en: A shudder ran down my back when the door opened.

et gæsteværelse.explanation: "Et gæsteværelse" means "a guest room", the room in your home for people who sleep over. It is built from gæst (guest) and værelse (room).

sentence.da: Du kan sove i vores **gæsteværelse**.
sentence.en: You can sleep in our guest room.

et gøremål.explanation: "Et gøremål" means "a chore", a small thing you need to get done, often at home or on a to-do list. It is mostly used in the plural: dagens gøremål (today's chores).

sentence.da: Jeg har mange **gøremål** i dag, blandt andet at handle og vaske tøj.
sentence.en: I have many chores today, including shopping and washing clothes.

gal.explanation: "Gal" means "crazy", for a person or idea that is mad or foolish. It also means "wrong" when something goes badly: Noget gik galt (Something went wrong), Det er galt (That is wrong).

sentence.da: Er du helt **gal**? Det er alt for farligt!
sentence.en: Are you completely crazy? That is far too dangerous!

galskab.explanation: "En galskab" means "madness" in the sense of a wild, reckless act or idea. It is usually about foolish behavior rather than a medical condition.

sentence.da: Det er rent **galskab** at sejle i den storm.
sentence.en: It is pure madness to sail in that storm.

galt.explanation: "Galt" means "wrong" and "bad": Jeg gjorde noget galt (I did something wrong). Before an en-word you use gal, which also means "crazy": en gal idé (a crazy idea).

sentence.da: Noget er **galt** med min computer.
sentence.en: Something is wrong with my computer.

gammel.explanation: "Gammel" means "old", for things (en gammel bil, an old car) and for a person's age. To ask age, you say Hvor gammel er du? (How old are you?) and answer Jeg er tredive år gammel (I am thirty years old).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er 90 år og meget **gammel**.
sentence.en: My grandfather is 90 and very old.

gammeldags.explanation: "Gammeldags" means "old-fashioned". Danish uses this one form with en-words, et-words and plurals. The opposite is moderne (modern).

sentence.da: Min mormor har et **gammeldags** køkken.
sentence.en: My grandmother has an old-fashioned kitchen.

gang.explanation: "Gang" means "a time" in the sense of an occasion: en gang means "once" and "to gange" means "twice". Gang can also mean a hallway in a house. Do not mix it up with tid (time in general). Hvor mange gange? means "How many times?".

sentence.da: Jeg har været i Paris en **gang**.
sentence.en: I have been to Paris once.

ganske.explanation: "Ganske" means "quite" or "fairly". It is weaker than meget (very), so ganske kold (quite cold) is less cold than meget kold (very cold).

sentence.da: Maden var **ganske** god, men lidt dyr.
sentence.en: The food was quite good, but a little expensive.
